arguments.value: Integrity and Time Life agreed to jointly create and co-brand the “Songs 4 Worship” series, a line of worship music compilations and companion songbooks. Integrity handles obtaining rights from third-party master owners, manufacturing the product, and selling product to Time Life; Time Life creates the artwork and pays mastering expenses. The product uses both companies’ names and logos, and each company has exclusive distribution rights in different channels: Time Life in general-market retail, catalogs, outgoing telemarketing, U.S. television direct response, and its own Internet/e-commerce channels; Integrity in Christian retail, direct mail, continuity sales, church sales, and Christian e-commerce channels. Time Life agreed to buy at least 10,000 units of each recorded product during the first 32 months after release, with an initial order of at least 5,000 units per recorded product. The parties also agreed to share mailing lists by equal-value names and to mutually agree on the retail release date. Integrity pays royalties to Time Life on Integrity’s sales, and Time Life pays royalties to Integrity on Time Life’s sales. The agreement includes trademark and copyright licensing, quarterly accounting and audit rights, indemnification, assignment rules, and other standard contract terms. The term runs from January 10, 2000 through December 31, 2004 unless extended in writing. The agreement says it is governed by Tennessee law, with disputes to be heard in state and federal courts in Nashville, Tennessee.
